preamble: Palatalization of the ejective sibilant: Hausa ts, pronounced [tsʼ] or [sʼ] depending on dialect, becomes the ejective affricate c' [tʃʼ] before front vowels in Western Hausa dialects, but not in Standard (Kano) Hausa (Newman 1996). It belongs to the general Hausa palatalization of alveolars before front vowels, in which t, s and z become c, sh and j. In Katsina and other Western dialects c' also occurs before a(a), where it contrasts with ts (c'àaki 'chicks' vs. tsàaki 'clicking sound in the throat', both tsàaki in Standard Hausa), so it is a separate phoneme there and not an allophone. The evidence is a single language and a single source, Newman (1996).

examples.note: Newman (1996: 539): before a(a) Western c' contrasts with ts, as in tsàaki 'clicking sound in the throat'.

sources: Newman, P. (1996). Hausa Phonology. In A. S. Kaye & P. T. Daniels (Eds.), Phonologies of Asia and Africa, 537–552. Eisenbrauns. https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/bitstream/handle/2022/21454/HausaPhonology.pdf

Newman, P. (2014). The Range and Beauty of Internal Reconstruction: Probing Hausa Linguistic History. Studies in African Languages and Cultures 48, 13–32. https://salc.uw.edu.pl/index.php/SALC/article/view/99
